newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tilburn likes his mousse clean and chops lean.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tilburn likes his mousse clean and chops lean.

text.p: Renowned small shareholder activist, Jack Tilburn, will celebrate his birthday on Friday with a bottle of mineral water and tray of lean chops, courtesy of Woolworths Ltd.

Tilburn jumped up and asked several questions about Woolworth's grocery operations at the group's annual meeting on Thursday, including one about its uncovered salad and dessert bars and one about the fat on Woolworth's short loin lamb chops.
Tilburn told the meeting about a recent visit to his local Woolworths supermarket at Dee Why in Sydney where he found what he said were very fatty lamb chops.
"It may have been incompetent butchery or just a very fatty carcass ... what can you say, Mr Chairman?," he said.
Woolworths chairman John Iliffe replied that Woolworths had a very good reputation for lean meat.
"I'm sorry if you've had any inconvenience. I'll personally see that a tray of well trimmed lamb chops will be delivered to you tomorrow," Iliffe said to loud applause from the meeting.
Earlier Iliffe had congratulated Tilburn, who regularly addresses annual meetings, on his 70th birthday due on Friday and said he would send him a bottle of champagne.
After Tilburn complained about the late-opening of Woolworths stores selling alcohol, Iliffe offered to send a bottle of mineral water instead.
Earlier Tilburn had also complained about the bulk food bars in Woolworths supermarkets, which have uncovered vats of chocolate mousse, coleslaw and salad.
A Woolworth's executive assured Tilburn that Woolworths was testing covered food bars.

Earlier another elderly shareholder had asked if Woolworths would ensure that in future its size six shoes had a dot or a dash under the six to make sure he and others did not buy them instead of size nine shoes.
